It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Last confirmed open: 8 June 2026. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Founded by brothers Ben and Joe Wright, Porta takes its cues from the neighbourhood bars of Spain: short menus, good produce, For the next Open Fire Dining Club , that Spanish influence is being taken out of Porta’s dining rooms and into the open air at Torr Vale Mill. Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said it was called to reports of a fire at Marc Darcy on Bury New Road in Salford at about 01:40 BST. The outlet was "well alight" when firefighters arrived and the blaze was tackled by eight fire crews and specialist units including a turntable ladder. A GMFRS spokeswoman said: "Crews remain in attendance as they continue to work to extinguish the fire and make the area safe." She added: "Bury New Road is currently closed by Greater Manchester Police and residents are asked to stay away from the area and keep doors and windows closed." An employee of the business, who did not want to be named, told the BBC staff "are very shocked". He said the business sold high-end men's designer suits and boasted several celebrities among their customers. James joins from global advisory firm Teneo, while Narjeet has moved from Lincoln International’s technology M&A team. Since launching in 2022, Northern Gritstone has reviewed more than 1500 investment opportunities and backed 52 life sciences and technology businesses across the North of England. Join us for a practical discussion on how to build effective AI governance that balances innovation with trust, accountability and risk management. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Education 'Changes are long overdue': The number of Greater Manchester teenagers not in education, employment or training In some parts of the region one in 20 teens are not in work or college News Annie Gouk and Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:59, 03 Aug More than 3,300 teenagers in Greater Manchester are not in education, employment or training (NEET), figures have revealed In some parts of the region one in 20, 16-17-year-old are thought to be 'NEETs'. In Salford , the borough with the highest proportion of NEETs, 363 young people are not in work or college Trafford , the area with the lowest rate, has just 184 teens classed as NEET. The figures come as Andy Burnham pledged to cut the number of jobless young people He made the commitment as he unveiled plans to open up new technical education routes to 14-year-olds, which will be put on an equal footing with traditional academic pathways. From Year 10, pupils will be able to combine core academic subjects, like English and maths, with techn The changes are 'long overdue', Mr Burnham said, adding that 'it's just not right' that the current system leaves young people not on the university pathway feeling 'that they’re some kind of second-class citizens'

A report of concern for Mr Swindells' welfare was made, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said. During the call, at around 7.40pm, his famil Police handcuffed Mr Swindells. Body worn camera footage shows officers saying that was done for his own safety, the watchdog said Mr Swindells then became unresponsive, the IOPC said, before receiving treatment at the scene. Officers began CPR at 8pm and paramedics arrived seven minutes later, the watchdog added. Officers gave CPR before North West Ambulance Service personnel took over Mr Swindells was taken to hospital, where he died the next day, Saturday, July 25. Greater Manchester Police said it is supporting the investigation. The force said Mr Swindells was 'restrained by officers responding to a report by family members of a man in crisis'

It is more than a week since the moorland fire began at Dovestone, while crews have been battling the Tintwistle fire for more than three weeks The fires have sent huge plumes of smoke over Greater Manchester and beyond. The Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service (DFRS) last night (Saturday) said a controlled burn would be carried out at Tintwistle This is set to cause an increase in smoke over the next 24 hours, the fire service said. It came, jurors heard, amid a feud between the Moston based 'M40' gang and the Rochdale and Oldham outfit Representing the Danger (RTD). My thoughts remain with the victims of these vile attacks "Today we are going further and providing record funding to help keep Jewish people in Manchester safe, supporting visible policing and protection around synagogues, schools and community centres. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires Greater Manchester's latest air quality map shows impact of raging moor fires across every borough It comes as residents living in the shadow of both fires have complained about the side-effects of the smoke Comments News Charlotte Fisher Report Two major incidents have been declared amid the fires at Dovestone and Swineshaw Reservoir , in Greenfield in Oldham and at Tintwistle Moor near Glossop. Dozens of firefighters remain at both scenes as smoke continues to billow into the air over our region On Wednesday, Paul Fearnhead, Incident Commander at the Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS), described the area near Dovestone as 'really, really challenging' as the 'extensive wildfire' continued He said: "Currently we have around just short of ten fire engines, including our wildfire capabilities at this scene and they’re deployed across the moorlands in this warm weather , which is being hampered by smoke and wind "If you're a member of the public in the area, we are asking you to stay away. It's a small area for us to work in, and the moors at this time are very smoky, and we'd ask you not to come across this area." Both fires are sending huge plumes of smoke across our region and beyond - with the latest air quality maps today (July 16) showing the ongoing impact the fires are having across Greater Manchester

Lucy Hobson, 33, will tackle Zinalrothorn later this month The 4,221-metre peak was first climbed in 1864, but Lucy is looking to make history when she tackles the mountain. Lucy has optic atrophy, a genetic condition where the optic nerves shrivel rather than form, which causes permanent vision loss While her condition has worsened over the years, Lucy refuses to let it stand in her way. "When I started doing these kinds of challenges, it was just for myself, really," she said "It is what I enjoyed, and it is what made me happy. I always suffered a lot with depression, and this helps me a lot "And then, aiming a bit higher... (I can) show people that if I can do it, if you're thinking about wanting to do something and there's something stopping you, just go and do it. Officers were called to reports of the incident on Norman Road near Broadoak Oasis Primary School on Saturday (August 1) According to Greater Manchester Police , the robbery occurred at around 3.40pm. Police say that three suspects approached the teenager and stole his bicycle. One of the assailants was carrying a large machete, according to reports It is understood the offenders made off along a footpath connecting Norman Road, Hall Road and Pollitt Avenue. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Four Border Force officers involved in Manchester Airport custody death still suspended from duty Dad-of-two Karl Joyce was found unresponsive in a holding area after being arrested at the airport Comments News Greta Simpson Senior The full inquest into a man who died after being arrested at Manchester Airport almost 18 months ago remains more than six months away, it emerged today (July 13) Karl Joyce, 27, was arrested by Border Force officers while going through security at the airport on February 19 2025 Later that same day Mr Joyce, a father of two from Fleetwood in Lancashire, was found ‘slumped in a chair’ in a holding area. He was believed to have swallowed ‘wraps’ of cocaine found in his underwear , the M.E.N previously reported He was taken to Wythenshawe Hospital where he died of cocaine toxicity, an inquest opening into his death heard last August . An IOPC investigation was launched shortly after and the four officers involved were suspended pending a disciplinary review At a pre-inquest review hearing held at Manchester Coroner’s Court today, senior coroner Zack Golombeck moved the full inquest to begin on February 22 next year - more than two years on from Mr Joyce’s death

More than 5.7million passengers are expected to fly in and out of the airport between Friday, July 17 and the end of the holidays on September 1 This equates to more than 120,000 passengers per day. It follows a record-breaking June, which saw the northern travel hub welcome more than three million passengers Those who are due to fly in the coming weeks are warned to plan their journey to the airport carefully due to major disruption to the tram network until August 2. Iram Ramzan repor News Iram Ramzan 22:30, 30 Jul 2026 Regional mayors will get a share of income tax revenue in what the Government says is the biggest transfer of power, funding and responsibility from Westminster in a generation The new system will give local leaders more freedom and flexibility to keep the revenue generated in their regions without being told by Whitehall how to spend it From April 2027, mayors will retain a greater share of business rates and from spring 2028 they will receive a share of income tax revenue. It is not yet clear what percentage of income tax the mayors will receive, but further details are expected during the autumn budget Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: “I said we'd take power out of Westminster and carry it into every postcode in the country. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford A promise to Salford people may soon be fulfilled Planning permission was granted for three tower blocks back in 2020 on the condition that the historic public baths were restored Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:57, 19 Jul 2026 Vi One of Salford's most famous sons learned to swim there. But for decades the Collier Street baths in Greengate has been an empty decaying shell Now it could have a new lease of life as Mackie Mayor style food hall which is housed in another historic building - Manchester's former Smithfield Market Hall on the edge of the Northern Quarter The listed former baths, built in 1855, is situated in the Colliers Yard development which was the former medieval heart of Salford. Renaker secured planning permission to build three tower blocks in 2020 on condition that the baths were restored The Cortland block was completed in October 2023 - a 50-storey tower with 559 rental apartments. In March 2025, Bankside followed in the form of a 43-storey building with 444 apartments. The third, Parkside, is expected to be 40 to 42 high storeys and deliver 420 to 444 apartment View 9 Images Collier Street Baths, Collier Street, Salford. 4th March 1989. (Image: Mirrorpix)

Plans to build 120 homes on the land were submitted last February by Manchester Metropolitan University (MMU) alongside housing developers Step Places and the Southway Housing A group known as the Ryebank Fields Community Group (RFCG) submitted an alternative application in August to ‘protect’ the land and use it as a community woodland and meadow. No decision has been made yet on either planning application Ryebank Fields Community Group said its submission to protect the land was supposed to be decided by the council in December but they are still waiting for an outcome. The group has written an open letter to town hall chief executive Tom Stannard asking for an explanation The letter reads: "We have contacted Manchester City Council on seven separate occasions seeking an update, a timetable for determination, and clarification of whether any outstanding matters remain "We have also offered a telephone conversation and a video meeting to assist in resolving any issues and facilitate progress. The organisation that runs them insists the tide is now turning View 7 Images Staff on s News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 05:58, 03 Aug 2026 As children returned to school from the Christmas holidays, staff joined picket lines outside the gates . Eight strike dates were called at Ravensfield and Lily Lane primary schools in January Teaching union NASUWT claimed that a 'culture of violence and intimidation' had led to frequent attacks on staff. It said that both pupil-on-teacher and pupil-on pupil assaults had 'grown to untenable levels' The union blamed leadership at both schools and the multi-academy trust which runs them. Changing Lives in Collaboration (CLIC), the trust which runs both schools, insisted that the allegations made 'did not reflect the day-to-day reality' at either academy It was a row that grabbed national headlines. Striking staff had the support of Manchester Evening News readers commenting on social media, and several parents of both current and former pupils at the two primary schools who spoke to the MEN It was just the beginning of a turbulent seven-month period for the two CLIC Trust schools. Ofsted inspectors handed down damning verdicts, a headteacher left her position, and the Department for Education (DfE) made two significant interventions

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Forest Bank Prison Sex offender died after taking overdose on first day in Forest Bank prison Gary Ogden had been convicted of sex offences the day before his death News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 15:16, 02 Aug 2026 View Image Forest Bank prison in Salf A sex offender died of a drugs overdose on his first morning in Forest Bank prison , a investigation has found David Ogden took an overdose of the painkiller oxycodone before he was found dead in his cell at the Salford jail. The day before the 44-year-old had been found guilty of sex offences following a trial at Manchester Crown Court and remanded to prison awaiting sentence It was his first time in jail and he was classified by staff as a 'vulnerable prisoner' who was 'significantly vulnerable to assault', a report by the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman (PPO) said. While at court, he was seen on CCTV putting something in his mouth Following his conviction, his mother said he had left a note in the dock saying he 'could not cope or carry on'. The note was never found or the contents verified On his arrival at Forest Bank Ogden, who was prescribed oxycodone for severe arthritis, was taken to shared cell. At 7am the next day, March 29, 2022, a healthcare assistant found Ogden 'unresponsive'. Paramedics were called and he was pronounced dead

Daud Nidhal Mohammed, 23, from Salford , was seen inhaling balloons filled with laughing gas at a petrol station moments before he drove his black Audi A5 over bright physicist and expert in x-ray technology Sam Johnston Mr Johnston, 28, returning from a general election party when he was hit just before 3am on July 5, 2024 As the University of Manchester masters graduate lay motionless at the junction of Trinity Way and Egerton Street, he was run over by a second car being driven by a blameless taxi driver. Mr Johnston suffered catastrophic injuries and died at the scene despite attempts to revive CCTV later viewed by police revealed Mr Johnston, who was wearing dark clothing, was seen to be unsteady on his feet and may have been wearing wireless headphones which were found nearby when he attempted to cross the road to go to his home nearby

One councillor said: “It’s all a bit of a farce from my perspective.” The change has been brought in because of safety issues caused by bin lids being open. In 2016, a Stockport bin man was left fighting for his life with a broken sternum and ribs after a bin dropped from the back of a lorry It is understood an open bin increases the risk workers might incorrectly place the bin on the back of the lorry due to poor visibility. Terry Lewis was elected as the Labour MP for Worsley in Salford in 1983 - a staunch socialist whose constituency included Salford's strongest Tory enclave He retired at the 2005 general election and was succeeded by Labour's Barbara Keeley. Mr Lewis, who was 69 when he retired from politics, once held the record for voting more than any other Labour MP against his own government, run at the time by Tony Blair After being a member for 44 years he quit the Labour Party in 2010 in disgust, saying it was close to 'Thatcherism', but rejoined in 2015 when Jeremy Corbyn became leader Mr Lewis, a born and bred Salfordian from Ordsall, served Labour as a councillor in Bolton and as a party worker before winning a seat in Parliament. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Derker 'The police knocked on every house on our road and not one of them would give any information' Life in Derker being a 'nightmare' is now over after a major police crackdown but there are fears a 'golden opportunity' is being wasted Comments New It was an area riddled with fear and violence. And it all brutally came home for Carol Knight when she found out her car had been firebombed - and the culprits were never found Carol’s car was firebombed in May 2023 in Derker, Oldham , in what she believes was a targeted attack. At the time, her daughter, Angela Cosgrove, was running for re-election as a councillor for the St James ward which covers the area - and Carol believes it was linked to that But despite the damage, Carol says ‘nothing seemed to get done’ as a result. “The sad thing is people were afraid of opening up," she said. "People were frightened about things coming back onto them “I didn’t feel any reassurance. Nothing whatsoever that the police were going to look into it. A lot of people will have known because we had been here for 70 odd years and people said if they do not look after you, what will they do to us? “That to me told me and my husband if they can’t do anything, why can I be bothered? That to me said something needed to be desperately done.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: That’s according to England talisman Harry Kane with the striking superstars set to face off tonight in a thrilling World Cup quarter-final. Haaland will lead the line for Norway with Kane set to skipper England in the 22:00 (UK) knockout clash at Miami Stadium. It’s a battle between two of the world’s most prodigious frontmen with not only progress to the last four up for grabs but also the competition’s Golden Boot in the balance with Kane on six and Haaland on seven behind only Argentina’s Lionel Messi and France’s Kylian Mbappe on eight in the fight for the prestigious individual gong. Heading into this evening’s hotly-anticipated encounter, Kane waxed lyrical about his opposite number. “Erling has been incredible,” said Kane. “Look at his goal scoring record. And physically, he’s a machine, he’s a beast. “His finishing is at another level and his goalscoring record speaks for itself. “I respect him a lot as a player and as a fellow professional. “I’m obviously hoping he has a quiet day. His performances speak for themselves. He’s a fantastic player.” The performances of both prolific forwards have led to comparisons and naturally questions of which player is better. It’s a discussion Kane refused to get drawn into primarily because he believes they’re different type of strikers. “It’s an impossible one for me to answer’” he added. “I think we are completely different players. I know we are both seen as strikers but we are almost two different positions if I’m totally honest.” City Magazine: World Cup special available now! Featuring Rayan Cherki, Erling Haaland, Omar Marmoush and a greatest ever World Cup Manchester Best XI - get reading now!
